title: Your balance
hook: worship, work, rest and family: give each its right (Bukhari)

segments.voice: Yesterday: khidmah, the sick room where Allah is found, and no thanks needed. Your line was serve.

Salman comes to visit his friend Abu al-Darda and finds Abu al-Darda's wife in shabby, careless clothes. What's wrong? he asks. Your brother, she says, has no interest in this world. Abu al-Darda puts food in front of his guest and says: eat, I'm fasting. Salman says: I won't eat unless you eat. So he eats. That night Abu al-Darda gets up to pray, and Salman tells him: sleep. Later he gets up again. Sleep, says Salman. Near the end of the night, Salman wakes him, and the two of them pray together. Then Salman says the line Sahih al-Bukhari keeps.
screen: `A WIFE IN SHABBY CLOTHES.` → `EAT. SLEEP.` → `THEN THEY PRAY TOGETHER.`

segments.voice: Your Lord has a right over you, your own self has a right over you, and your family has a right over you, so give each one its right. When they told the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, what had happened, he said: Salman has spoken the truth. Notice who was out of balance. Not a lazy man. A devout one, fasting through the day and rising to pray through the night, while his wife sat in shabby clothes. Too much of a good thing had pushed something else out. Another report in Bukhari tells it a second way. The Prophet hears that the companion Abdullah ibn Amr fasts every day and prays every night, and tells him: fast and break your fast, pray and sleep, for your body has a right over you, your eyes have a right over you, and your wife has a right over you. Eyes have a right. Sleep isn't a lapse in devotion. It's owed. Why it holds together: the Qur'an says, in Pickthall's words, "Allah tasketh not a soul beyond its scope." A practice that breaks the person practicing it isn't what was asked. These weeks you've met a diverse ummah, asked the questions of today, and built a practice for today, one piece at a time. Balance is what keeps all of it standing. Not everything every day. Each thing its right.
screen: `GIVE EACH ONE ITS RIGHT.` · `A DEVOUT MAN, OUT OF BALANCE.` · `YOUR EYES HAVE A RIGHT.` · `NOT BEYOND ITS SCOPE.`

segments.voice: Go through the four rights one at a time and give each a breath: worship, where it has a place in your day; work, what it asked of you today; family, one face, one need; and yourself, your body, your eyes, how tired they are. Notice which one got crowded out this week, no blame, just notice. If you pray, thank Allah for the day in your own words.
Your balance. Giving your Lord, yourself, your family and your work each their right, so none crowds out the rest. Today's word.
Your line: give each its right. This block ends here, and the year starts gathering itself in. Rest well tonight.

howItsDone: Muslims cite the hadith of Salman and Abu al-Darda, 'give each one its right', as a guide to balancing worship, work, rest and family, so that devotion does not crowd out sleep, health or the rights of a spouse and children.

chat.says: I've been fasting and praying so much I barely sleep. Isn't more always better?
options: Not if it crowds out the rest. Your body and eyes have a right over you.
Yes. The more you fast and pray, the better, with no limit at all.
Yes. Sleep is a lapse in devotion that the devout learn to give up.

notes: Confirm Sahih al-Bukhari 1968 for the Salman and Abu al-Darda story and the paraphrase of its details (Umm al-Darda's clothes, the meal, waking to pray near the end of the night).
Confirm Sahih al-Bukhari 1975 for the Abdullah ibn Amr report (body, eyes and wife each have a right).
The outline hook lists 'worship, work, rest and family'; the hadith itself names the Lord, the self and the family. The script keeps work from the outline; check.

Editor: the teach and fork said Abu al-Darda fasted 'every day' and prayed 'all night', which Sahih al-Bukhari 1968 does not state (it shows him fasting that day and rising at night; 'fasts every day' belongs to the Abdullah ibn Amr report); reworded in the teach, match and fork, and 'his wife quietly stopped caring how she looked' now keeps to the report's shabby clothes.
